First beta of 0.16.0. Everything below is meant to ship in v0.16.0 once it survives a test pass - install this to help catch what doesn't, and expect a v0.16.0-beta.2 when it does.

### Highlights

- **Zabbix as a monitoring engine.** An existing Zabbix answers for a site's monitoring status, alongside or instead of Danbyte's own checks. Add a connection (frontend URL, a named API token), create an engine of kind *Zabbix*, bind it to a device, site or location, and put a *Zabbix* check on the addresses it should answer for - the same templates, intervals, history, alert rules, silences and notification channels every other check has. Zabbix's trigger severities map onto Danbyte's states per connection. **Provisioning**, off by default, writes Danbyte's inventory back: hosts named and addressed from the device, host groups and templates from stacking rules on role, platform, type or maker, an SNMP interface when the device has an SNMP profile, and - behind its own switch - the community as a Zabbix secret macro. *Review* mode proposes every write for approval; *Auto* applies; pruning of hosts Danbyte itself created is a third switch with a grace period. Each poll also brings back the host's **open problems** and which protocols Zabbix **cannot reach it on**, shown as chips beside the roll-up badge and in full on the address's Monitoring section - a host whose SNMP interface polls nothing reads healthy otherwise. (#162)
- **Search overhaul.** ⌘K / Ctrl+K opens a command palette; one ranked list comes back across every object type instead of twenty boxes. Accents and case are folded (`aarhus` finds `Århus DC`), typos still land, exact names rank first, an IP lists the prefixes containing it, and tokens narrow the query: `type:device site:aarhus role:core status:active tag:dc`. Every hit shows its status pill and where it sits. Settings pages and individual settings are findable from the same palette. (#89, #51)
- **Backup and restore.** Settings → Backups: encrypted `.dbk` archives of the database, media and non-secret configuration, to a local directory or an S3-compatible bucket, on schedules with retention. Restore from the same page with a preview, a typed confirmation and a protected *Before restore* archive; the upgrade scripts take a *Before upgrade* backup through the same engine and stop when it fails. (#27)
- **Scripts.** Python that reads and writes your data through the API, as you - run from a button or a schedule, with parameters, a live log and downloadable output. Sandboxed child processes, a short-lived per-run token, and *trusted* scripts with ORM access behind their own permission. (#65)
- **Agent access and Ask Danbyte.** Danbyte speaks the Model Context Protocol at `/api/mcp/` for Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or your own agent, with the token's exact access and a second switch for writes. And a chat panel in the top bar answers questions about your own network, showing every lookup it made - connect Anthropic, any OpenAI-compatible service, or a local Ollama or LM Studio so nothing leaves the box. Both off until you turn them on. (#11)
- **Monitoring policies match on more.** Policies can now scope to a **region** (reaching every site below it), a **site** (including addresses with no device on them) or a **platform**, on top of VRF, device type, role, device and prefix. Any policy can be narrowed by a device **name glob**, by **tags** the device must carry, or by the **interface** an address is bound to. The resolver's precedence is documented, including where a prefix policy's mask length lands in the ladder.
- **Spec sheets.** A device, VM or virtual chassis page has a Spec sheet button that opens a printable A4 PDF datasheet - elevations, stat boxes, details with custom fields, modules and inventory, interfaces with MAC vendor, VLAN, IPs and cable peer. (#150)
- **Settings, rebuilt.** One catalog drives the settings navigation, hub, search and assistant. Pages are grouped by subject, every body is a card, integrations and plugins are toggle cards on one page with vendor marks, and the golden-standard Admin page layout is the norm everywhere. (#51)

### Monitoring

- **Every result and status change says who answered** - Danbyte's own workers, an Outpost by name, or Zabbix - as a Source column on the Checks list (filterable) and on every history row. It is the engine that ran the check, not the one the target is bound to.
- **A history API.** `GET /api/monitoring/transitions/` reads status changes back filtered by anything an address is - site, region, device type, role, platform, VLAN, prefix, VRF, port, tag, check kind, source - with facet counts and a bucketed series in the same answer; per-object and timeline endpoints turn the same log into status-over-time segments for strips, the uptime figure now integrates those same segments, and the results chart takes a 24h / 7d / 30d window.
- **Status history you can see.** A **History** tab on Monitoring lists every status change with a rail that filters by state, source, type, site, device type, role, platform, check, engine, region, device, prefix, VRF, VLAN, tag or port - counts on every facet - over 24h to 90d or a custom range, charted per hour or day, saved as views, exported. An address's Monitoring tab draws each check's last seven days to scale and carries a History panel with the changes behind the strip; a device gets a Monitoring tab of its own (the SNMP facts keep theirs, now called SNMP) with the roll-up strip, one strip per address, and the same panel. The Overview's results chart takes a 24h / 7d / 30d window and its recent changes are grouped by the hour they landed in.
- **The Checks list on the same rail.** Facets with counts for status, source, type, site, device type, role, platform, check and engine; region, device, prefix, VRF, VLAN, tag and port pickers; server-side sorting on every column; address rows carry DNS name, device and site; a *7 days* switch draws each row's status strip; saved views and export. The device page's roll-up and Overview show what Zabbix reports about the host - open problems, protocols it cannot reach - as the lists do.

- **Your own names for the six check states.** A status can *speak for* a check state: tick it on the status form, pick Up / Degraded / Down / Unknown / Stale / Skipped, and that status's name and colour replace the shipped ones everywhere monitoring is shown - the Monitoring column and its split badge, roll-ups, the filter rail, the dashboard charts, and the Zabbix severity picker. One status per state; the stored value stays the state, so alert rules and webhooks are untouched.
- **A check kind registered by an integration or plugin is selectable** in the Add-check dialog, the template editor, alert rules and silences. The list comes from the checker registry rather than a hard-coded set.
- **An engine can be bound to one device**, not only a site or location - "this switch is watched by Zabbix, the rest of the building is ours". Resolution is device → location → prefix → site → tenant default → local.
- **A driver engine answers its own kind only**; a target's other checks (an ICMP ping on a Zabbix-bound device) still run on Danbyte's workers. Before, nothing claimed them and they never ran.
- Telegram as a notification channel; Microsoft Teams channels send an Adaptive Card instead of Slack's payload.
- Policy resolution no longer re-queries per policy per address, and an address stored with a mask matches its enclosing prefixes again.

### IPAM & DCIM

- **NAT rules** document what a firewall translates - source, destination, translated address, ports, direction - as a first-class object with its own statuses. (#151)
- **A VLAN ID is unique per site, not per tenant**, and VLAN resolution across SNMP drift and virtualization sync goes through one resolver that refuses to guess between ambiguous candidates. (#159)
- **MAC vendors** from the IEEE OUI registry, with your own ranges, overrides and *Next free in range*; a proper MAC detail page; VM interface MACs in the registry. (#141, #142)
- **SNMP for virtual chassis** - a stack polled once through its master, drift split per member, an SNMP tab on the stack page. (#148)
- Module-type interface templates take `[1-24]` ranges. (#147)
- Foreign keys that were plain text are links across lists and detail pages; catalog badges keep their colour and become the link.

### Topology & maps

- **Zones on the topology map** - draw a labelled, coloured box around a group of nodes, drag and resize it, and **remove devices from a custom view** by right-click. Zones belong to the view they were drawn on and never leak to the global map.
- **The site map can hide roles, regions and sites**; hiding a site takes its cables and circuits with it, whether or not they have a drawn route.
- Tunnels draw to virtual machines; circuit cables keep the map alive.

### Integrations

- **Virtualization sync options** (#160): per-source switches to sync VM interface MTU, skip offline VMs, and - off by default, with a grace period - remove guests the hypervisor no longer reports. Danbyte does not delete a VM unless asked.
- Hypervisor sync is one toggle per kind; a kind whose sync is off is hidden and refused.
- **Azure Key Vault as a secret store** for issuance keys and device credentials, with the token audience derived from the vault's own host so sovereign clouds work by URL alone. The secret store is pluggable. (#58)
- Directory logins get what their groups say: an LDAP mapping can grant superuser and its tenants land on the profile at login. API tokens can be read-only.

### Everyday interface

- Settings are searchable from the global palette - cards rank above pages and deep-link to the card.
- Confirmation before deleting an attached image; Updates uses the shared page shell; the agent-access and notification pages scroll.
- The **Sites** list counts devices and VMs alongside prefixes and VLANs, so a site's size reads off the row.
- **Watched endpoints can be filtered.** A search box over the host, SNI name and certificate subject, plus a filter rail for status, port, monitoring on/off and an *expires in* range - so "which certificates expire within 30 days" is one number, and expired ones are in the answer rather than hidden in a band. Saved views work here like every other list. (#161)
- Dashboard donut legends follow the **widget's** width, not the screen's: a narrow tile on a wide monitor puts the legend below the chart instead of running it off the card. (#156)
- An interface's addresses are separated by a divider - `10.0.0.1 | 10.0.0.2` - instead of running together, wrapping so table rows stay level. (#149)
- **Sync interface MTU** no longer appears on a vCenter source: vSphere puts MTU on the vSwitch, not on a VM's vNIC, so the option could never act there. (#160)
- **Zabbix adoption rules** place an adopted host by its name, host group or address - `kbh-*` to København, `regex:^odense-` to Odense, a CIDR to a site - the same matcher the VM placement rules use. First match wins; a rule sets only what it names, and the review queue says which rule placed a host. Every proposal in that queue now also names the system that changes - *Create in Zabbix*, *Adopt into Danbyte* - because a host group called "Danbyte estate" made the old wording read backwards.
- **Zabbix provisioning can follow the rules instead of the checks.** Pick *Every device the rules match* and Danbyte keeps Zabbix's host list in step with the inventory while still doing its own pinging, discovery and TLS checks - the hybrid arrangement where Danbyte is the source of truth and Zabbix is fed from it. *Every device* now means every device, not every device somebody had already bound to a Zabbix engine by hand. Devices with no address are counted and reported rather than silently skipped.
- Picking several things from one catalog - Zabbix templates, say - no longer closes the list after each choice: it keeps its place, clears the search, shows a checkbox per row and offers select-all over whatever you have searched for.

### Fixes

- A Zabbix engine was reported *unreachable* while every one of its checks was answering on time: it was never marked as seen, since only an Outpost's phone-home did that, and it was judged by an Outpost's poll interval. It is now seen each time it reaches Zabbix - and not when it cannot - and judged by its own checks' cadence.
- The status donut on the Monitoring page wrapped its legend as three-and-one; it is balanced in pairs now.

- The Zabbix integration toggle on Settings → Integrations saved nothing - the serializer listed its fields by hand and left it out. Every integration toggle is now derived from the registry, with a test that holds the two together.
- An Outpost's writes to audited models raised in the audit signal and were lost. An Outpost is recorded by name with no linked user.
- A masked address matched no prefix policy and no inherited assignment.
- Cable ends carry their site, so a hidden site's undrawn cables disappear with it.

### Upgrading

- Migrations apply automatically: search index and extensions (`api.0157`–`0160`), VLAN scoping (`api.0161`), NAT rules (`api.0162`), monitoring statuses (`api.0163`), read-only tokens and LDAP superuser grants (`auth_api.0022`–`0023`), the secret-store registry, post-upgrade notices, AI and Azure settings (`core.0048`–`0051`), integration toggles and virt-sync options (`integrations.0038`–`0042`), Telegram, driver engine kinds, device engine bindings, policy scopes and filters, and the check-state detail (`monitoring.0082`–`0089`), and the new `agents`, `assistant`, `backups`, `scripting` and `zabbix` apps.
- PostgreSQL `pg_trgm` and `unaccent` are created by migration; PG 13+ needs no superuser for them.
- A Zabbix server on an internal address must be added to the outbound allow-list under Settings → Security before Danbyte will reach it.
- One post-upgrade step for systemd installs with a hand-managed nginx config: the `/api/backups/` location for large archives. It appears on Settings → Updates until marked done.
- The container image carries `postgresql-client-17` for backup and restore.
